text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:
- The governor of the Bank of Slovenia France Arhar is attending the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund meeting in Washington on Monday and Tuesday.
- Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic is visiting Slovenia on Monday where he will meet his counterpart Zoran Thaler, President Milan Kucan and Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek.
- The sport and cultural organisation said the new tobacco law, introduced last November, slashed their income due to the prohibition of sponsorship by tobacco firms.
- A Slovenian sanitary army group, consisting of 27 people, will join international peace groups in Albania in the first half of May, the army said.

- Parliament is expected this week to determine a date for a referendum on whether to limit the amount of forests, nationalised after the Second World War, that would be returned to their previous owners.
- The government has not yet outlined a national energy programme where it would determine its long-term plan of the development of energy suppliers.
- Over 66 percent of Slovenians support the politics of the government of Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, an opinion poll showed.
- The Ministry of Legislation said it would detail the current law on money laundering in line with the requirements of the European Union.
